evidence.title: Lovable: Overview; What is not available on mobile
evidence.locator: Overview; What is not available on mobile
evidence.finding: Lovable provides native iOS and Android apps using the same account, projects and credits as its web app. Mobile has no offline editing, cannot create accounts or configure OAuth connectors, and omits narrow-screen preview tools.

evidence.title: Lovable: Credits and usage
evidence.finding: A workspace subscription pools build credits for its projects and collaborators. Free has daily allowances; paid plans add monthly subscription credits and top-ups.

evidence.title: Lovable: How to use Build mode
evidence.finding: Users describe a project or change in chat; the hosted builder explores the code, edits files and runs checks without a local environment setup.

evidence.title: Lovable: Lovable MCP server
evidence.finding: The official MCP server lets external AI tools interact with Lovable projects using authenticated tools.

evidence.title: Lovable: Custom MCP servers
evidence.finding: Lovable can connect to custom MCP servers so the agent can access external tools and information.

evidence.title: Lovable: How to use Build mode
evidence.finding: Natural-language prompts initiate project changes in the project chat. This is not proof of a separate issue backlog.

evidence.title: Lovable: Review and edit a plan
evidence.finding: Plan mode investigates without changing code and produces a plan users can edit, revise and approve before Build mode. Planning costs one credit plus any subagent research.

evidence.title: Lovable: Project knowledge
evidence.finding: Project knowledge provides persistent instructions and context for Lovable across project requests.

evidence.title: Lovable: November 4, 2026: Dreaming
evidence.finding: Paid-plan Dreaming checks memory and AGENTS.md rules against code and chat, rewrites or removes outdated notes and records AGENTS.md changes in chat and history. User-requested rules stay as written.

evidence.title: Lovable: How subagents work
evidence.finding: Read-only subagents can search files, inspect project code, perform lookups and browse the web, returning findings to the main agent. Their context is limited to their brief.

evidence.title: Lovable: Can multiple subagents run at once?
evidence.locator: Can multiple subagents run at once?
evidence.finding: Lovable can run multiple read-only research subagents concurrently on independent questions. They cannot edit, create or delete project files.

evidence.title: Lovable: Subagent types; How subagents work
evidence.finding: Lovable starts Generic and Explore read-only subagents, displays their status and inspected steps, and receives their findings automatically. Subagents report to the main agent and do not communicate directly with each other.

evidence.title: Lovable: Send follow-ups mid-build; Control the cost
evidence.locator: Send follow-ups mid-build; Control the cost
evidence.finding: Users can send steering follow-ups while a build runs or stop it. Credit exhaustion pauses work with resume or wrap-up options, and completed edits remain after a stop.

evidence.title: Lovable: Draft statuses
evidence.finding: The draft switcher shows working, updates available, new changes, needs input and failed states, with shared All drafts and My drafts views. This is draft navigation, not proof of an epic backlog.

evidence.title: Lovable: How Lovable works on a goal
evidence.locator: How Lovable works on a goal
evidence.finding: A /goal Build message continues toward an outcome for up to ten hours, accepts follow-ups and still pauses for credit check-ins or needed access.

evidence.title: Lovable: Overview; Offline use
evidence.finding: Web and mobile clients operate on the same hosted projects and require an active network connection. The source does not establish that a build always continues after client disconnect.

evidence.title: Lovable: Create a draft; Update a draft
evidence.locator: Create a draft; Update a draft
evidence.finding: Each draft is a separate project copy with its own chat and preview. Changes reach the main unpublished project only after acceptance; newer main changes can be brought into a draft. No container, VM or worktree boundary is asserted.

evidence.title: Lovable: Accept the draft; Delete a draft
evidence.locator: Accept the draft; Delete a draft
evidence.finding: Accepted drafts enter project history. Deleting a draft removes its edits and cannot be undone. Process recovery after host loss is not documented here.

evidence.title: Lovable: How long Lovable works on one message; Cost controls
evidence.locator: How long Lovable works on one message; Cost controls
evidence.finding: Build messages run up to ten hours and wrap up during the last half hour. Credit check-ins default to twenty credits and pause for a decision; the stop button halts work.

before.answer: Lovable provides native iOS and Android apps using the same account, projects and credits as its web app. Mobile has no offline editing, cannot create accounts or configure OAuth connectors, and omits narrow-screen preview tools.

after.answer: Lovable provides native iOS and Android apps using the same account, projects and credits as its web app. Mobile has no offline editing, cannot create accounts or configure OAuth connectors, and omits narrow-screen preview tools. changes.summary: Establish shared prompting through account-based project editor invitations and the shared project chat. Preserve unknown simultaneous-input ordering and optional independent drafts.

before.answer: Invited project collaborators build in the same project using the owner workspace credits; each can work in a separate draft. This establishes shared editable projects, not simultaneous input ordering on one agent.

after.answer: Distinct Lovable accounts invited as project Editors can build in the shared project and access its editor/chat. Each project contains the chat used to instruct Lovable; optional drafts make a separate copy with its own chat. Simultaneous input ordering remains unestablished.
